title: Electromagnetic force (তড়িৎ চৌম্বক বল)
placement: Book page 68, topic 3.2.2: তড়িৎ চৌম্বক বল বা বিদ্যুৎ চৌম্বকীয় বল (Electromagnetic Force), next to that paragraph.
description: The electromagnetic force (তড়িৎ চৌম্বক বল, page 68, 3.2.2) in two examples. চিরুনি, the book's own experiment: the student drags a comb through a student's hair (or presses চুল আঁচড়াও); each stroke leaves a little charge on it (blue − discs on the comb, a five-step আধান meter, loose hairs stand up towards it). Brought to bits of paper on the desk (কাগজের কাছে আনো: it flies there and comes down slowly, or drag it), the bits jump up and cling to it once the comb is close enough (farther with more charge), and the comb lifts them up into the air. The bit under the comb's last teeth (the first to jump) carries two arrows: পুরো পৃথিবীর টান (down, মাধ্যাকর্ষণ বল, purple) and চিরুনির টান (up, তড়িৎ চৌম্বক বল, blue), growing as the comb comes closer; the panel compares them live (< or >) and, once the paper is lifted, says that the comb's tiny charge beats the whole Earth's pull, and that the book says the force is 10^36 times as strong as gravity. A comb with no charge lifts nothing. চুম্বক: a 1.5 V cell, a knife switch and a coil of copper wire on a plastic tube in a row, and a bar magnet (N red, S grey) on a little cart. Switch on: chevrons run along the wires (the current) and the coil becomes a magnet (its ends named N and S): electric and magnetic forces are one force. Unlike poles attract, like poles repel (turn the magnet round by tapping it, or drag it), with equal and opposite arrows at the facing ends that shrink along the whole track but never vanish (range infinite); a corner note says the coil's pull is drawn stronger than a real one. The panel also shows the four fundamental forces in order, weakest to strongest, with তড়িৎ চৌম্বক highlighted and each one's range. Test: 5 tap questions (why the paper rises or what an uncharged comb does; like or unlike poles; the coil with the switch open; which force is stronger and by how much; whether the coil still pulls the magnet at the far end of the track), each with a worked answer and, for most, a note on the mistake. Phone-first, Bangla. GLB: the comb scene (student, comb, bits of paper on the bench) and the magnet scene (cell, switch, coil, bar magnet on its cart), life size: modelled in mm, exported in metres (no arrows or labels).
